<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|HOLY weeke. 272|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XIX.}}</noinclude>tooke his garments (and they made foure partes, to euery souldiar a part) & his coate. And his {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Mt. 27. 35. Mr. 15, 24. Luc. 23, 34. · This coate vvithout seame is a figure of the vnitie of the Church. ''Cypr. de vnit. Ec''. And Euthymius and other write that our Lady made it.}}∷ coate vvas vvithout seame, wrought from the toppe through out.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=24}}† They said therfore one to an other, Let vs not cut it, but let vs cast lottes for it vvhose it shal be. That the scripture might be fulfilled saying, ''They haue parted my garments among them: and vpon my vesture they haue cast lottes''. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 21, 19.''}}* And the souldiars did these things.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=25}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Gospel in a votiue Masse of our B. Lady betweene Easter & Whitsuntide.}}∷ And there stoode beside the crosse of {{sc|Iesvs}}, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The great loue faith, courage, compassion, and sorowes, that our Lady had: who forsooke not the Crosse and her sonne, when so many were fled from him, and his cheefe Apostles denied him.}}∷ his mother, and his mothers sister, Marie of Cléphas, and Marie Magdalene. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=26}}† VVhen {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore had seen his mother and the disciple standing vvhom he loued, he saith {{sup|‖}} to his mother: VVoman, behold thy sonne. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=27}}† After that, he saith {{sup|‖}} to the disciple, Behold thy mother. And from that houre the disciple tooke her to his ovvne.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=28}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Psa. 68, 22.''}}* Aftervvard {{sc|Iesvs}} knovving that al things vvere novv consummate, that the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel in a votive Mass of the Passion.}}scripture might be fulfilled, he saith, I thirst. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=29}}† A vessel therfore stoode there ful of vinegre. And they putting a spongeful of vinegre about hyssope, offered it to his mouth. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=30}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore vvhen he had taken the vinegre, said, It is consummate. And bovving his head, he gaue vp the ghost.

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=31}}† The Ievves therfore (because it vvas the Parasceue) that the bodies might not remaine vpon the crosse on the Sabboth (for that vvas a greate Sabboth day) they desired Pilate that their legges might be broken, and they might be taken avvay. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=32}}† The souldiars therfore came: and of the first in deede they brake the legges, and of the other that vvas crucified vvith him. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=33}}† But after they vvere come to {{sc|Iesvs}}, vvhen they savv that he vvas dead, they did not breake his legges, {{verse|chapter=19|verse=34}}† but one of the souldiars vvith a speare opened his side, and incontinent there came forth {{sup|‖}} bloud and vvater. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=35}}† And he that saw it, hath giuen testimonie: and his testimonie is true. And he knovveth that he saith true, that you also may beleeue. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=36}}† For these things vvere done that the scripture might be fulfilled, ''You shal not breake a bone of him''.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 12, 46.''}} {{verse|chapter=19|verse=37}}† And againe an other scripture saith, ''They shal looke on him whom they pearsed''.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Zac. 12, 10.''}}

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=38}}† And after these things {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''* Mt. 27, 57. Mr. 15, 42. Lu. 23, 50.''}}* Ioseph of Arimathaea (because he vvas a disciple of {{sc|Iesvs}}, but secrete for feare of the Iewes) desired Pilate that he might take avvay the body of {{sc|Iesvs}}. And Pilate permitted. He came therfore, and tooke avvay the body of {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=39}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 3, 1. 7, 50.''}}* Nicodemus also came, he that at the<noinclude>{{rh|||first}}</noinclude>
